name: Subword vocabulary induction
characteristic: criterion by which the next vocabulary item is chosen
positive_test: fits a finite token vocabulary to a corpus before any model is trained
negative_test: a fixed hand-written vocabulary or a whitespace split with no induction step
examples: BPE, WordPiece, Unigram LM
notes: tokenizer choice is reported as a method, not a library setting

name: Byte-pair-encoding merges
positive_test: merges the most frequent adjacent pair, iteratively, to a target vocabulary size
negative_test: likelihood-driven vocabulary pruning
examples: BPE, byte-level BPE, SentencePiece-BPE

name: Likelihood-gain merges
positive_test: merges the pair that most increases corpus likelihood under a unigram model
negative_test: pure frequency counting
examples: WordPiece

name: Vocabulary pruning from a superset
positive_test: starts from a large candidate set and removes items that cost least likelihood
negative_test: bottom-up merging
examples: Unigram LM, SentencePiece-Unigram

name: Tokenizer-free byte or character units
positive_test: uses raw bytes or characters, so no vocabulary is induced from data
negative_test: any corpus-fitted vocabulary
examples: ByT5 scheme, CANINE scheme, character-level LM input
notes: boundary: arguably the absence of an algorithm

name: Input-space data augmentation
characteristic: what is transformed and how the transform is chosen
positive_test: replaces or perturbs a training example with a transformed version, leaving the label rule intact
negative_test: transformations applied at test time only; architectural noise layers
examples: RandAugment, CutMix, SpecAugment

name: Geometric and photometric transforms
positive_test: applies a fixed hand-specified image transform family with sampled parameters
negative_test: transforms whose parameters are themselves learned or searched
examples: random resized crop, horizontal flip, rotation, color jitter
notes: named weakly; include only when the paper names the recipe

name: Occlusion and erasing
positive_test: deletes a contiguous region of the input and does not replace it with other data
negative_test: mixing two examples together
examples: Cutout, Random Erasing, GridMask, token dropout

name: Example mixing
positive_test: builds a training example by combining two or more examples and their labels
negative_test: single-example perturbation
examples: mixup, CutMix, Manifold Mixup, FMix, Mosaic, AugMix
notes: label is mixed too, which also touches the objective

name: Searched augmentation policies
positive_test: selects which augmentations to apply by searching over policies against a validation signal
negative_test: a fixed augmentation list chosen by hand
examples: AutoAugment, Fast AutoAugment, RandAugment, TrivialAugment, PBA
notes: sits on two axes at once by construction; S.src.meas + S.form.metric pinned in D.1: searches an augmentation policy by a measured held-out score

name: Text-space augmentation
positive_test: perturbs tokens or re-generates text while preserving the label
negative_test: prompt engineering at inference
examples: EDA, back-translation, synonym substitution, round-trip translation

name: Adversarial example generation
positive_test: constructs an input perturbation that maximises the model's loss under a norm budget
negative_test: random noise with no maximisation step
examples: FGSM, PGD, C&W, AutoAttack
notes: same procedure serves as attack and as training-data source

name: Class-imbalance resampling
characteristic: whether examples are added, removed or synthesised
positive_test: changes the class frequencies seen by the learner, without changing the loss definition
negative_test: a reweighted loss, which is an objective change
examples: SMOTE, ADASYN, Tomek links, NearMiss, random oversampling

name: Dataset curation and selection
characteristic: what score decides whether an example is kept, ordered or weighted
positive_test: selects, deduplicates, weights or orders the training examples before or during fitting
negative_test: generating new examples; transforming individual examples
examples: SemDeDup, DoReMi, curriculum learning

name: Near-duplicate removal
positive_test: removes examples that are near-identical to another under a similarity threshold
negative_test: removing examples for being low-quality rather than redundant
examples: MinHash/LSH dedup, SemDeDup, exact-substring dedup

name: Quality and contamination filtering
positive_test: drops examples scored below a threshold by a classifier, perplexity model or rule
negative_test: dropping examples to balance classes
examples: quality classifier filtering, perplexity filtering, decontamination

name: Domain mixture weighting
positive_test: chooses sampling proportions across labelled data sources
negative_test: choosing which single corpus to use
examples: DoReMi, DoGE, hand-tuned domain weights

name: Curriculum ordering
positive_test: changes the order or schedule in which examples are presented, not which are present
negative_test: changing the set of examples
examples: curriculum learning, self-paced learning, anti-curriculum, sequence-length warmup

name: Active and coreset selection
positive_test: repeatedly selects which unlabelled points to label or keep, using the current model
negative_test: a one-shot random subsample
examples: uncertainty sampling, BALD, core-set selection, GraNd, EL2N

name: Dataset distillation
positive_test: optimises a small synthetic dataset so that training on it reproduces training on the full set
negative_test: compressing the model rather than the data
examples: dataset distillation, gradient matching, distribution matching

name: Classical feature preprocessing
characteristic: what statistic of the training data the transform is fitted to
positive_test: fits a fixed transform to the training split and applies it to every split
negative_test: a transform with no fitted parameters
examples: z-scoring, ZCA whitening, target encoding

name: Location-scale and whitening transforms
positive_test: removes mean and rescales or decorrelates using first and second moments
negative_test: rank-based transforms
examples: standardisation, min-max scaling, PCA whitening, ZCA whitening

name: Rank and quantile transforms
positive_test: maps values through their empirical rank or quantile
negative_test: moment-based rescaling
examples: quantile normalisation, rank-gauss, Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson

name: Discretisation and encoding
positive_test: converts a continuous or categorical column into a new coded representation
negative_test: continuous rescaling
examples: equal-width/equal-frequency binning, MDLP, one-hot, target/mean encoding

name: Missing-data imputation
positive_test: fills missing entries with values estimated from observed data
negative_test: dropping incomplete rows
examples: mean/median imputation, MICE, kNN imputation, matrix-completion imputation

name: Feature selection
positive_test: removes input variables before or during fitting based on a relevance score
negative_test: projecting features into a new space
examples: mutual-information filtering, recursive feature elimination, lasso selection, Boruta

name: Synthetic training-data generation
characteristic: what produces the synthetic example
positive_test: creates new training examples from a model, a simulator or a rule, rather than transforming real ones
negative_test: perturbing an existing real example
examples: Self-Instruct, domain randomisation, Evol-Instruct

name: Model-generated corpora
positive_test: a generative model emits the training examples, optionally filtered
negative_test: a human or simulator emits them
examples: Self-Instruct, Alpaca-style generation, Evol-Instruct, synthetic textbooks
notes: overlaps distillation when the generator is a stronger model

name: Simulation and domain randomisation
positive_test: a simulator with randomised parameters emits examples to cross a reality gap
negative_test: data collected in the target domain
examples: domain randomisation, procedural scene generation, sim-to-real pipelines

name: Counterfactual example construction
positive_test: constructs an example differing in one causal factor while holding others fixed
negative_test: arbitrary perturbation with no factor held fixed
examples: counterfactual data augmentation, CAD, minimal-pair generation

name: Exploration rules
characteristic: what quantity drives the deviation from the greedy action
positive_test: decides which action to take for the purpose of gathering data, separately from the update rule
negative_test: a rule that defines the learning target rather than action selection
examples: epsilon-greedy, UCB1, RND
notes: the single most under-named slot in RL papers

name: Undirected stochastic exploration
positive_test: perturbs the greedy action with noise that does not depend on uncertainty
negative_test: noise scaled by a learned or counted uncertainty
examples: epsilon-greedy, Boltzmann/softmax, OU noise, parameter-space noise, NoisyNets

name: Optimism under uncertainty
positive_test: adds a confidence bonus to value estimates and acts greedily on the inflated value
negative_test: sampling from a posterior instead of inflating
examples: UCB1, UCB-V, LinUCB, optimistic initialisation, RLSVI

name: Posterior sampling
positive_test: samples a hypothesis from a posterior and acts greedily with respect to it
negative_test: adding a deterministic bonus
examples: Thompson sampling, bootstrapped DQN, posterior sampling for RL

name: Intrinsic-motivation bonuses
positive_test: adds a learned novelty or prediction-error term into the reward the agent optimises
negative_test: a bonus used only for action selection and never entering the return
examples: RND, ICM, pseudo-counts, Disagreement, NGU, empowerment
notes: also alters the objective, so it carries two roles

name: Diversity-driven and archive-based search
positive_test: maintains an archive of behaviours and explicitly selects for behavioural novelty
negative_test: selecting for return only
examples: Go-Explore, novelty search, MAP-Elites, DIAYN, DADS

name: Experience storage and relabelling
characteristic: what decides which past transition is reused and with what target
positive_test: stores past interaction and re-serves it to the learner, possibly with a changed target
negative_test: generating fresh interaction
examples: uniform replay, PER, HER

name: Uniform experience replay
positive_test: samples stored transitions uniformly at random
negative_test: sampling with a priority or a changed goal
examples: experience replay, replay ratio schedules

name: Priority-weighted replay
positive_test: samples stored transitions in proportion to a learning-progress score
negative_test: uniform sampling
examples: PER, ERE, LAP, topological replay

name: Goal and reward relabelling
positive_test: rewrites the goal or reward of a stored transition so a failure becomes a success
negative_test: reusing a transition with its original reward
examples: HER, hindsight relabelling, GCSL relabelling

name: Opponent and task generation
characteristic: what determines the opponent or task distribution
positive_test: generates the training distribution by playing against or generating versions of the system itself
negative_test: a fixed opponent or fixed task set
examples: self-play, PSRO, PLR
notes: S.src.meas + S.form.metric pinned in D.1: selects or generates opponents and tasks by a measured win rate or learning progress

name: Self-play against current or past selves
positive_test: plays the learner against copies of itself drawn from its own training history
negative_test: playing against a fixed scripted opponent
examples: naive self-play, fictitious self-play, self-play with opponent pools

name: Population and league training
positive_test: maintains a population with explicit exploiter or niche roles and matchmaking
negative_test: a single-copy self-play loop
examples: PSRO, double oracle, AlphaStar league, NFSP

name: Automatic environment curricula
positive_test: generates or selects environments or goals to match the agent's current competence
negative_test: a fixed environment distribution
examples: POET, PLR, ADR, ALP-GMM, asymmetric self-play

name: Dynamic programming for MDPs
positive_test: computes a value or policy by sweeping Bellman backups over a known transition model
negative_test: learning from sampled transitions without a given model
examples: policy iteration, value iteration, generalised policy iteration, asynchronous DP
notes: founder of the whole value-based lineage

name: Temporal-difference learning
positive_test: updates a value estimate toward a bootstrapped target built from the next state's own estimate
negative_test: updating toward a full Monte-Carlo return only
examples: TD(0), TD(lambda), true online TD, GTD

name: Off-policy TD control
positive_test: bootstraps from the max (or an argmax-decoupled estimate) over next-state actions
negative_test: bootstrapping from the action the behaviour policy actually took
examples: Q-learning, Double Q-learning, Expected SARSA(off-policy form)

name: On-policy TD control
positive_test: bootstraps from the action the current policy actually selects
negative_test: bootstrapping from a max over actions
examples: SARSA, Expected SARSA, n-step SARSA

name: Deep Q-networks
positive_test: fits Q-learning with a neural network plus a target network and a replay buffer
negative_test: tabular Q-learning; actor-critic with an explicit policy head
examples: DQN, Double DQN, Dueling DQN, NoisyNet-DQN, Rainbow, Ape-X, R2D2, Munchausen DQN
notes: the canonical "ancestor worth aggregating to"

name: Distributional value learning
positive_test: learns the full return distribution rather than only its expectation
negative_test: learning a scalar expected return
examples: C51, QR-DQN, IQN, FQF

name: Sample-efficient deep value learning
positive_test: raises updates-per-environment-step with explicit remedies for the resulting overfitting
negative_test: scaling data rather than updates
examples: DrQ, SPR, SR-SPR, BBF, REDQ
notes: SPR is multi-parent with self-predictive SSL

name: Policy-gradient methods
attributes: A.world.free; A.hier.flat; A.agents.single; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: differentiates expected return with respect to policy parameters via the score-function identity
negative_test: updating a value table or network with no explicit policy parameterisation
examples: REINFORCE, actor-critic, A3C, A2C

name: Actor-critic
positive_test: reduces policy-gradient variance with a learned value baseline or critic
negative_test: using an empirical return baseline only
examples: actor-critic, A3C, A2C, GAE, IMPALA/V-trace, ACER

name: Trust-region and clipped policy updates
positive_test: bounds the size of the policy change per update by a divergence or ratio constraint
negative_test: an unconstrained gradient step on the policy
examples: natural policy gradient, TRPO, PPO, PPO-clip, V-MPO
notes: value_parent derived from denials: {'L.pg.ac': 0, 'L.precond.trust': 4}; dead denials dropped: value_parent means the contradicting parent no longer propagates; dead denials dropped: value_parent means the contradicting parent no longer propagates; dead denials dropped: value_parent means the contradicting parent no longer propagates

name: Group-relative policy optimisation
positive_test: replaces the learned critic with a baseline computed across a sampled group of completions
negative_test: using a learned value network as the baseline
examples: GRPO, RLOO, DAPO, Dr.GRPO
notes: the dominant recent RL-for-reasoning branch

name: Deterministic policy gradients
positive_test: backpropagates the critic's gradient through a deterministic actor
negative_test: sampling actions from a stochastic policy and using the score function
examples: DPG, DDPG, TD3, D4PG
notes: requires continuous actions

name: Maximum-entropy RL
positive_test: optimises return plus a policy-entropy term as part of the objective, not as a bonus
negative_test: entropy added only as an auxiliary regulariser with no soft-Bellman consistency
examples: soft Q-learning, SAC, MPO, soft actor-critic variants, REDQ

name: Model-based RL
characteristic: what the learned dynamics model is used for
positive_test: learns a transition or reward model and uses it to improve the policy or the value estimate
negative_test: learning a value or policy directly from environment samples only
examples: Dyna, PETS, Dreamer, MuZero

name: Model-generated experience
attributes: A.world.learned; A.regime.off; A.agents.single; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: uses the learned model to synthesise extra transitions for a model-free learner
negative_test: using the model only inside an action-selection search
examples: Dyna, Dyna-Q, MBPO, SLBO

name: Model-predictive control over a learned model
positive_test: re-plans an action sequence at each step by rolling the model forward
negative_test: amortising the plan into a policy network and never re-planning
examples: PILCO, PETS, CEM-MPC, MPPI, iCEM

name: Latent-dynamics world models
attributes: A.world.learned; A.regime.off; A.rltarget.ac; A.agents.single; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: learns dynamics in a compressed latent space and trains the policy inside it
negative_test: planning directly in observation space
examples: World Models, PlaNet, Dreamer, DreamerV2, DreamerV3, TD-MPC

name: Learned-model tree search
attributes: A.regime.off; A.rltarget.ac; A.hier.flat; A.deriv.first; A.deriv.comb; A.determinism.stoch; A.param.param; A.world.learned; A.outspace.disc; A.cadence.mini
positive_test: combines a learned model with an explicit tree search that produces the acting policy
negative_test: planning by trajectory sampling without a tree
examples: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, MuZero, EfficientZero, Sampled MuZero
notes: the clearest case of one lineage spanning two roles

name: Offline reinforcement learning
attributes: A.regime.offline; A.world.free; A.hier.flat; A.agents.single; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
characteristic: how the policy is kept inside the data's support
positive_test: learns a policy from a fixed logged dataset with no further environment interaction
negative_test: collecting new interaction at any point in training
examples: BCQ, CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer

name: Explicit policy constraint
positive_test: penalises or projects the learned policy toward the behaviour policy
negative_test: penalising the value function instead
examples: BCQ, BEAR, TD3+BC, BRAC

name: Pessimistic value penalty
positive_test: lowers values of out-of-distribution actions so they are never selected
negative_test: constraining the policy's action distribution directly
examples: CQL, COMBO, pessimistic MDPs, EDAC

name: Implicit and weighted-regression policy extraction
positive_test: extracts a policy by advantage-weighted regression without querying unseen actions
negative_test: computing a max over actions outside the data
examples: AWR, AWAC, IQL, XQL, SQL

name: Return-conditioned sequence modelling
positive_test: casts control as supervised next-token prediction conditioned on a desired return
negative_test: fitting a value function and improving a policy against it
examples: Decision Transformer, Trajectory Transformer, RvS, Multi-Game DT
notes: signal is a label, not a reward, despite being RL

name: Imitation learning
characteristic: what replaces the reward signal
positive_test: fits a policy from expert demonstrations with no environment reward
negative_test: learning from an environment reward signal
examples: behaviour cloning, DAgger, GAIL

name: Behaviour cloning
attributes: A.regime.offline; A.world.free; A.rltarget.policy; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: fits actions to states by supervised regression or classification on demonstrations
negative_test: inferring a reward function first
examples: behaviour cloning, DAgger, DART, ACT, diffusion policy training

name: Inverse reinforcement learning
positive_test: infers a reward function that rationalises the demonstrations, then plans or learns on it
negative_test: directly copying actions
examples: MaxEnt IRL, guided cost learning, AIRL, Bayesian IRL

name: Adversarial imitation
attributes: A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.rltarget.ac; A.param.param; A.uncert.point; A.determinism.stoch; A.world.free; A.agents.single; A.hier.flat
positive_test: trains a discriminator to separate agent from expert transitions and uses it as reward
negative_test: matching actions pointwise
examples: GAIL, DAC, AIRL, f-GAIL

name: Preference-based alignment
characteristic: whether a reward model is fit, and how the policy is updated against preferences
positive_test: optimises a policy against pairwise or ranked human or AI preference judgements
negative_test: optimising against a scalar reward supplied by the environment
examples: RLHF, DPO, GRPO-with-reward-model
notes: attributes migrated: A.outspace.struct -> A.outstruct.*, federated party values -> A.parties.*

name: Reward modelling plus policy optimisation
positive_test: fits an explicit reward model on comparisons, then runs an RL algorithm against it
negative_test: optimising the policy on preferences in closed form, with no reward model
examples: RLHF with PPO, RLAIF, Constitutional AI, reward-model ensembles

name: Direct preference optimisation
positive_test: derives a closed-form policy loss from the preference pairs, skipping the reward model
negative_test: fitting a separate reward network
examples: DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO, cDPO, CPO

name: Rejection-sampled finetuning
positive_test: samples candidates, keeps the best by a scorer, then does supervised finetuning on them
negative_test: updating with a policy-gradient step
examples: best-of-n finetuning, RAFT, STaR, rejection-sampling SFT, ReST
notes: sits between SFT and RL

name: Verifier-rewarded RL
positive_test: the reward comes from a programmatic checker rather than a learned or human judgement
negative_test: a reward model trained on human comparisons
examples: RLVR, unit-test reward, math-answer-match reward

name: Multi-agent RL
characteristic: how the joint value or joint policy is factored
positive_test: trains two or more interacting policies whose returns depend on each other
negative_test: a single agent in a stationary environment
examples: QMIX, MADDPG, MAPPO

name: Independent learners
positive_test: each agent runs a single-agent algorithm treating others as part of the environment
negative_test: any explicit factorisation of a joint value or a centralised critic
examples: IQL, IPPO, independent A2C

name: Value factorisation
attributes: A.agents.coop; A.obsmode.ctde; A.rltarget.value; A.outspace.disc; A.regime.off; A.world.free; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: decomposes a joint action-value into per-agent terms under a monotonicity or additivity condition
negative_test: learning the joint value without any decomposition
examples: VDN, QMIX, QTRAN, QPLEX, Qatten

name: Centralised critic, decentralised actors
attributes: A.agents.coop; A.obsmode.ctde; A.rltarget.ac; A.world.free; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
positive_test: trains a critic with access to global state while each actor sees only its own observation
negative_test: both training and execution use only local information
examples: MADDPG, MAPPO, COMA, FACMAC

name: Equilibrium-computing methods
positive_test: computes an approximate equilibrium rather than a best response to fixed others
negative_test: optimising against a frozen opponent
examples: fictitious play, CFR, Deep CFR, NFSP, Nash-Q, regret matching

name: Hierarchical RL
attributes: A.hier.hier; A.agents.single; A.world.free; A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param
characteristic: what the temporal abstraction is defined over
positive_test: learns a policy over temporally extended sub-policies with their own termination
negative_test: a flat policy over primitive actions
examples: options framework, option-critic, FeUdal networks, HIRO, HAC

name: Bandit algorithms
characteristic: how uncertainty about arm values is turned into a choice
positive_test: selects among actions with immediate feedback and no state transition
negative_test: a setting with state dynamics and delayed credit
examples: UCB1, Thompson sampling, EXP3
notes: shares its characteristic with L.explore by design

name: Stochastic and contextual bandits
attributes: A.regime.on; A.guar.regret; A.outspace.disc; A.agents.single; A.cadence.one; A.param.param
positive_test: assumes i.i.d. rewards per arm, possibly conditioned on a context vector
negative_test: an adversarial reward sequence
examples: UCB1, LinUCB, LinTS, Thompson sampling, KL-UCB

name: Adversarial bandits
positive_test: guarantees regret against an arbitrary, possibly adaptive reward sequence
negative_test: an i.i.d. reward assumption
examples: EXP3, EXP4, Tsallis-INF

name: Best-arm identification
positive_test: spends a fixed budget to identify the best arm, not to maximise cumulative reward
negative_test: minimising cumulative regret while acting
examples: successive halving, sequential halving, LUCB, racing
notes: had L.hpo.bandit as a second parent, which made a 2-cycle; the edge runs HPO -> BAI only

name: Off-policy evaluation and learning
positive_test: estimates the value of a policy from logs collected under a different policy
negative_test: evaluating a policy by running it
examples: inverse propensity scoring, self-normalised IPS, doubly robust OPE, FQE
notes: shares estimators with causal inference

name: Instance-discrimination contrastive learning
positive_test: pulls together views of the same instance and explicitly pushes apart other instances
negative_test: a method with no negative examples in its loss
examples: InstDisc, CPC, MoCo, MoCo v2, MoCo v3, SimCLR, SimCLR v2

name: Cross-modal contrastive alignment
positive_test: contrasts paired items from two different modalities against mismatched pairs
negative_test: contrasting two augmented views of one item
examples: CLIP, ALIGN, SigLIP, AudioCLIP, ImageBind
notes: pairing is a supervision source, which blurs self vs supervised

name: Label-aware contrastive learning
positive_test: treats all same-class examples as positives using ground-truth labels
negative_test: treating only augmented views of one instance as positives
examples: SupCon, contrastive representation distillation

name: Negative-free self-distillation
positive_test: regresses a student view onto a target produced by a momentum or stop-gradient copy
negative_test: a loss containing explicit negative pairs
examples: Mean Teacher, BYOL, SimSiam, DINO, DINOv2
notes: collapse avoidance is the defining engineering problem

name: Redundancy-reduction objectives
positive_test: decorrelates embedding dimensions via a cross-correlation or covariance criterion
negative_test: contrasting whole embeddings against other samples
examples: Barlow Twins, VICReg, VICRegL, W-MSE

name: Clustering-based self-supervision
positive_test: alternates assigning pseudo-cluster labels and predicting them from another view
negative_test: a loss defined directly between embeddings with no assignment step
examples: DeepCluster, SeLa, SwAV, PCL, ODC

name: Masked-input prediction
characteristic: what is masked and what the reconstruction target is
positive_test: hides part of the input and trains the model to recover it from the remainder
negative_test: predicting the next element with no masking of a visible context
examples: BERT MLM, MAE, wav2vec 2.0

name: Masked language modelling
attributes: A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param; A.uncert.point; A.determinism.stoch; A.outspace.disc
positive_test: masks tokens and predicts their identity from bidirectional context
negative_test: predicting only the next token left to right
examples: CBOW, BERT MLM, RoBERTa, SpanBERT, T5 span corruption, ELECTRA
notes: ELECTRA replaces the target with a detection task

name: Masked visual modelling
positive_test: masks image or video patches and reconstructs pixels, tokens or features
negative_test: reconstructing the whole unmasked image
examples: Context Encoders, BEiT, MAE, SimMIM, iBOT, VideoMAE

name: Masked and contrastive speech modelling
positive_test: masks spans of audio and predicts quantised or clustered units
negative_test: predicting transcribed text
examples: wav2vec, wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, WavLM, data2vec

name: Handcrafted pretext tasks
positive_test: invents a label from a known transformation of the input and predicts it
negative_test: predicting part of the raw input content itself
examples: relative patch position, jigsaw, rotation prediction, colourisation, shuffle-and-learn
notes: largely historical; kept as an aggregation ancestor

name: Latent predictive self-supervision
positive_test: predicts the representation of unobserved content rather than its raw content
negative_test: regressing raw pixels or tokens
examples: CPC, I-JEPA, V-JEPA, SPR, PBL
notes: SPR applies this inside RL, hence multi-parent

name: Shallow embedding induction
characteristic: what co-occurrence structure the embedding factorises
positive_test: fits a lookup-table embedding directly from co-occurrence statistics, with no deep encoder
negative_test: training a deep encoder end to end
examples: word2vec, GloVe, fastText, DeepWalk, node2vec, item2vec
notes: produces a model, but the procedure is the entry

name: Autoregressive density modelling
positive_test: factorises the joint density into a product of conditionals and fits each by maximum likelihood
negative_test: fitting a bound on the likelihood or an implicit density
examples: n-gram MLE, neural LM, PixelRNN, PixelCNN, causal LM pretraining, WaveNet training
notes: the dominant pretraining objective; needs its own ancestor; attributes migrated: A.outspace.struct -> A.outstruct.*, federated party values -> A.parties.*

name: Exposure-bias corrections

positive_test: changes which context the model conditions on during training to match inference
negative_test: plain teacher forcing
examples: scheduled sampling, professor forcing, SeqGAN-style corrections

name: Variational autoencoding
positive_test: maximises an evidence lower bound with an amortised inference network
negative_test: maximising exact likelihood; using a discriminator
examples: wake-sleep, VAE, beta-VAE, IWAE, NVAE

name: Discrete-latent autoencoding
positive_test: quantises the latent to a learned codebook and trains through a straight-through estimator
negative_test: a continuous Gaussian latent
examples: VQ-VAE, VQ-VAE-2, VQGAN, FSQ, RQ-VAE
notes: the tokeniser for most latent generative stacks

name: Adversarial generative training
characteristic: which part of the minimax setup is altered
positive_test: trains a generator against a discriminator whose loss it maximises
negative_test: any objective with an explicit likelihood or reconstruction term
examples: GAN, WGAN, StyleGAN, CycleGAN

name: Adversarial divergence variants
attributes: A.deriv.first; A.cadence.mini; A.param.param; A.uncert.point; A.determinism.stoch; A.outspace.cont

characteristic: what is reorganised so the operator fits the device's memory hierarchy
positive_test: recomputes a standard operator with a different memory-access or scheduling pattern, emitting the same values
negative_test: a different operator (linear or sparse attention changes the function and is model-side); a package shipping such a kernel

name: Tiling and fusion of a fused operator
positive_test: splits the operator into blocks kept in fast memory, fusing the steps so no large intermediate is written out
negative_test: recomputation purely to save activation memory across layers (L.memtrade)
examples: FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, FlashDecoding, fused layer-norm

name: Inference cache management
